newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power up on weather, outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power up on weather, outages.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Southeast rose Monday on warm weather in parts of the region and reduced generation capacity available due to weekend outages, said market sources.
"There were offers that were higher, but there was little energy that moved at those levels," said a Southeast-based power marketer.
Areas of the deep South were forecast to experience temperatures in the high 80's and low 90's Fahrenheit range today and Friday.
Duke Power Co expected its 846 megawatt (MW) Oconee 2 nuclear unit in Seneca, S.C., to resume service midweek after being manually shut down to repair a valve.
Carolina Power and Light Co began coasting down operation of its 767 MW Brunswick 1 nuclear station in Southport, N.C., for a 35-day refueling program.
Florida Power Corp's 825 megawatt Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level. Fla., remained shut following repairs to a leaky section of line that feeds lubrication oil to the unit's turbine shaft.

In the Southeastern Reliability Council (SERC), non-firm power for heavy demand hours on Tuesday was quoted at $15.75-$17.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) for delivery into the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority, compared with Friday's quote of $16.50 for Monday.
Peak power at southern TVA was valued near $20.00. up from a range of $17.50-$18.00 on Friday.
TVA itself was heard offering Tuesday peak electricity at $20.50.
At the Georgia/Florida border, peak, non-firm electricity was quoted at $20.00-$23.50, a wider quote than Friday's $20.00-$20.50 value for delivery on Monday.
